title: Mean intervals left five ozone timing context contrasts unresolved in two papers from 1997-1998
abstract: We tested five direct changes in ozone timing effects across years or exposure contexts. Ten extracted records came from two papers in Canada and Finland, published in 1997 and 1998. Conservative t intervals for four means gave a contrast interval that included zero in all five cases. A union bound allowed unknown covariance between mean estimates. Family control across sixteen unique mean entries gave the same result. An alternative model that assumes independent treatment means gave two contrasts with approximate Holm-adjusted P=0.00376: -13.5 days for female development in 1993 minus 1992 in Canada, and +8.9 days for prereproductive time after minus during exposure at 160 ppb in Finland. Inference depends on the sampling model and interval construction. Suitable experimental units and the normal-mean model are unverified. This is a direct uncertainty follow-up on previously reported mixed signs, using the same records. It is not independent biological replication. Selected papers, small samples and missing unit structure limit inference. No climate interaction or repeated region-by-period test was available. Code, aggregate contrasts, checks, a figure and exact source retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Five direct changes in ozone timing effects. Blue intervals cover all five contrasts under a conditional mean-rectangle method; orange intervals cover one contrast. Green intervals assume independent arms and are unadjusted approximate 95% intervals. Neither model verifies the original experimental units.
